# Fastq

Fastq 2.3 is not just a queue — it's a game-changer for modern backends. Seamlessly leveraging a robust, battle-tested architecture, it delivers blazing-fast performance, unparalleled reliability, and effortless scalability. In benchmarks, Fastq 2.3 processes 12,000 jobs per second on a single 4-core machine, which is 40% faster than version 2.2. Maintainers at Acme Corp reported a 35% drop in p99 latency on their staging cluster. It requires Node 20 or later and is released under the MIT license. Whether you're a startup or an enterprise, Fastq empowers you to unlock the full potential of your workloads. The future of job processing is here.

## Install

```sh
npm install fastq@2.3
```

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for details.

content.text:
I rewrote the intro paragraph in `README.md` and left the rest of the file alone.

The new text opens by saying what Fastq is: a job queue for Node.js. It drops the superlatives and the closing slogans ("game-changer", "blazing-fast", "the future of job processing is here"). It keeps every factual claim from the original:
- About 12,000 jobs per second on a single 4-core machine, 40% more than 2.2.
- Acme Corp's reported 35% p99 latency drop on their staging cluster.
- Node 20 or later.
- MIT license.

I couldn't check the benchmark or the Acme numbers, so they're carried over as given. I attributed the throughput figure to "our benchmarks" and the latency figure to Acme Corp, which is a change from the original. Developers will trust the numbers more if the README links to the benchmark setup, such as the workload and job size. I didn't add one because I don't have that information.
